_note: Worked-example data only. The feature, ticket keys, hosts and scope names below are invented (ADR 3): swap in your own ticket and prototype when running these.

evals.prompt: Ticket QAP-XXXX 'เพิ่มรหัสโปรโมชัน (Add new Promo Code)' is pasted below with its acceptance criteria. The design prototype is at https://prototypes.example.com/app/index.html#promo-code-settings . Produce QA test cases in our Test Case template, focused only on what the ticket describes.
assertions: Every acceptance criterion in the ticket (AC-ADD-01 … AC-ADD-18) maps to at least one test case; none is dropped.

The workbook reproduces the team's template layout: both sheets in the template's own order and names, the header on the template's header row, data starting the row after it, the running-number formula, the test-type and priority data validations, and the header fill.
TC IDs follow <AREA>-<FEATURE>-NNN and are unique and sequential (PROMO-CODE-SETTING-…).
Steps and expected results are numbered multi-line strings (`1. …\n2. …`), not single blobs.
Cases that depend on a spec-vs-prototype disagreement are flagged in the note column with a marker and a question reference, while normal cases carry the template's own 'normal case' wording.
The default output is the workbook only; the gap report / open-questions list is stated in the chat (or written to a .md only if the user opted in), each question phrased as a decision for the team.
No case is invented for prototype-only features absent from the ticket (e.g. the edit flow), unless the ticket includes them.
No extra side files (JSON source, gap report) are written unless the user asked for them.
The prototype base URL is taken from the link in the prompt and passed to fetch_prototype.py; the script is never called expecting a built-in default.

evals.prompt: (same ticket) Cover the matching rule: one promo code may hold any number of discount-tier values for a single campaign type, and within a Region a (campaign type, tier) pair maps to exactly one promo code.
assertions: There is a case asserting the tier dropdown hides values already paired for that (Region, campaign type).
There is a case asserting a fully-paired campaign type yields an empty dropdown (no selectable value).
There is a case asserting the same campaign type is independent across Regions (pairing in Region A does not hide options in Region B).
There is a case asserting changing the campaign type clears already-selected tiers and reloads the options.
There is a case asserting a same-tier-different-weekday branch (e.g. Friday 10%, other days 5%) contributes each distinct daily value as its own separate option.

evals.prompt: Ticket QAP-1041 '[Catalog][Promo] ตั้งค่ารหัสโปรโมชัน — Add Promo Code' with its AC is pasted. Prototype: …/#promo-code-settings . Make the test cases.
assertions: Before generating, the assistant works out the workbook naming convention from the team's existing files (or asks), proposes a concrete name, and asks the user to confirm the ticket key and card name.
The assistant does not assert a naming pattern it did not read or confirm.
Before generating, the assistant proposes a TC ID prefix and asks the user to confirm it or choose another (suggestion offered as an option).
Before generating, the assistant asks whether the user wants the optional side files (JSON source, gap report) and defaults to workbook-only.
The assistant does not pick a file name, TC ID prefix, or write extra files on its own without asking.
The generated workbook file name matches the pattern the user confirmed, with the ticket key and card name in it.

evals.prompt: Run scripts/build_workbook.py over a small cases.json and confirm the workbook opens and matches the template contract.
assertions: Output opens with openpyxl; the sheet names and their order match references/template-format.md.
The header row's cells equal the documented headers across all twelve columns.
The first data row's running-number cell holds a formula referencing the test-type cell beside it.
The `test` defined name exists and the test-type and priority column data validations are present.
freeze_panes matches the documented cell and each case became exactly one data row with its TC ID in the TC ID column.
